main_body: Two stacked or adjacent wooden crates: a large one at the back-left and a smaller one at the front-right. Each has a striped plank top and a dark brown front face with a diagonal brace.
top_band: Light tan #b98a55 alternating with mid #99683a plank stripes, rows 1-8 at x=15 (L 113-146), about 8 rows tall; a dark edge row at row 9.
evidence: The column at x=15 reads as a light striped top (rows 1-8, L 113-146), a dark step at row 9 (L=44), then a front face at rows 10-17 (L=65) with a diagonal brace, then a dark base at rows 18-19. The step between top and front is over 80 L, so the top is a clear horizontal surface that is about as tall as the front face. That makes the lid read as a crate top seen from above. The front brace is painted flat rather than inset, but the top, the dark edge row and the front face are all clearly drawn. No isometric side face is shown.

style.evidence: The piece has only 8 distinct colours and a median of 6 per tile, against 17-20 per tile and 38-40 colours in the references. The material ramps are shallow: the top alternates between two tans, and the front face is one flat brown plus a thin brace line and a dark base. The outline is a dark brown tint (only 12% neutral edge pixels), which is acceptable. The plank stripes give some texture, but there are no grain dots, speckle or per-plank highlights, so it looks noticeably thinner and flatter than the Beodeul crates and props.
